newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Most Australian wheat pool prices held steady.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Most Australian wheat pool prices held steady.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board increased its estimates of pool prices for two classes of wheat in the 1996/97 crop but has held all other prices steady.
The estimated pool prices of 1996/97 Prime Hard and Australian Hard wheat were each increased by A$5.00 a tonne to A$250.00 and A$235.00 a tonne respectively, the AWB said.
The estimated price of 1996/97 Australian Standard White (ASW) was maintained at A$215.00 a tonne.
Estimates prices for all grades of 1995/96 wheat were steady, with ASW held at A$252.00 a tonne.
AWB general manager merchandising Ron Storey said the new prices reflected the difference in prices for higher protein wheat now becoming evident in the international market.

There was growing concern about the quality of U.S. Soft Red Winter (SRW) wheat crop. Infestations of vomitoxin had been found in the wheat and buyers were shifting their attention to other higher protein grades, he said.
In the last two weeks the difference in price between SRW wheat futures had contracted while in the higher protein Hard Red Winter wheat they had grown by A$6 a tonne.
"I'm also expecting that a big U.S. white wheat crop will compete with our ASW and lower grades of wheat," he said.
The U.S. crop had developed into an excellent crop creating an added market force in determining protein premiums, he said.
Prices listed were for the normal pool, but growers using the extended payment pool option could anticipate an additional A$3 to A$4 a tonne, he said.
Growers using the extended payment pool option would get 40 percent of the estimated value of the crop at harvest instead of the normal 80 percent of value.
The next pool price revision will be on September 9.
